4393.stem:
Ali has a credit card which has no interest-free period. Interest is charged at $13.5\%$ per annum, compounding daily, on the amount owing.

During the month, Ali made only one purchase of \$450 using the credit card. The full amount owing was repaid 21 days later.

parts.latex: Calculate the amount of interest charged on the purchase, assuming that interest is charged for the 21 days.
What percentage of the full amount repaid is the interest? Give the answer to two decimal places.

solutions.latex:
Daily compound interest uses a rate of $\dfrac{13.5}{365}\%$ per day for 21 days.
$$\begin{aligned}A &= 450\left(1+\dfrac{0.135}{365}\right)^{21}\\ &= \$453.51\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Interest} &= 453.51-450\\ &= \$3.51\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Substitutes some correct values into the compound interest formula, or equivalent merit

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex: $$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage} &= \dfrac{3.51}{453.51}\times 100\\ &\approx 0.77\%\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct percentage
Attempts to do a percentage calculation, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Nisa has a credit card on which interest at $17\%$ per annum, compounded daily, is charged on the amount owing.

At the beginning of the month, Nisa owes \$500 on her credit card. She makes no other purchases using the credit card, but fifteen days later, she repays \$250.

Assuming that interest is charged for the fifteen days, calculate the amount owing on the credit card immediately after the \$250 payment is made.

solutions.latex:
Using compound interest with daily rate $\dfrac{0.17}{365}$ for 15 days, then subtracting the repayment:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Amount owing} &= 500\left(1 + \dfrac{0.17}{365}\right)^{15} - 250 \\ &\approx \$253.50 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Applies the compound interest formula correctly, or equivalent merit
Attempts to apply the compound interest formula, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Chris has a credit card on which interest is charged at $15\%$ per annum on the amount owing and compounding daily.

On 14th June, Chris owes $\$950$ on his credit card. He makes no further purchases using the credit card. The period for which the interest is charged includes the date of purchase and the date of payment. Calculate the amount owing on the card on 12th July.

solutions.latex:
The daily rate is the annual rate divided by 365.
$$r = 0.15\div 365 \approx 0.0004109$$
Interest is charged from 14 June to 12 July inclusive of both dates, so
$$n = 29$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Amount} &= 950(1+0.0004109)^{29} \\ &\approx \$961.39 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Correct $r$ and $n$, or equivalent merit

The credit card charges interest at 19.5% per annum, compounding daily.

How much does Bikash owe on the credit card after 30 days of interest has been added to the balance and no other purchases or repayments have been made?

solutions.latex:

$$\begin{aligned} FV &= PV(1+r)^n \\ &= 5560\left(1 + \dfrac{0.195}{365}\right)^{30} \\ &= \$5649.81 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Bikash owes } \$5649.81$$
criteria: Correct answer

parts.latex:
Bobbie is charged $0.04\%$ compound interest per day on outstanding balances on a credit card. Bobbie has an outstanding balance of \$740 for 30 days.

Which of the following is an expression for the amount of interest Bobbie is charged?

solutions.latex:
The daily rate is $0.04\%=0.0004$, compounded daily for 30 days. This is not divided by 365 because the rate is already per day.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= P(1+r)^n \\ &= 740(1+0.0004)^{30} \end{aligned}$$
The interest is the final amount less the original balance.
$$\text{Interest}=\$740(1+0.0004)^{30}-\$740$$
Hence the answer is D.
criteria: Correct answer

meta.self_check: Compound interest formula, interest = A - P.
meta.generated_note: MCQ working written from the answer key.

parts.latex:
A credit card has an interest-free period of 45 days from and including the date of purchase. Interest is charged on purchases made, compounding daily at a rate of $13.74\%$ per annum, from and including the day following the interest-free period.

Concert tickets were purchased for a total of \$392 using this credit card.

Full payment was made on the 68th day from the date of purchase. There were no other purchases on this credit card.

What was the total interest charged when the account was paid in full?

solutions.latex:
The interest-free period is 45 days, so interest applies for
$$68 - 45 = 23 \text{ days}$$
Using the compound interest formula with daily rate $\dfrac{13.74\%}{365}$:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \$392\left(1 + \dfrac{0.1374}{365}\right)^{23} \\ &= \$395.41 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Interest charged} &= \$395.41 - \$392 \\ &= \$3.41 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Uses the compound interest formula with correct $r$, or equivalent merit
Attempts to use the compound interest formula, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Rihana uses a credit card for her purchases. The card has an interest rate of $18.5\%$ per annum, compounding daily with no interest-free period. Interest is calculated on the balance owing from the purchase date (included) until the last day of the month.

During April, Rihana makes the following purchases and payment.

\extable{497_q31_t1}

Calculate the closing balance on this credit card on the 30th of April.

solutions.latex:
Interest compounds daily at $\dfrac{0.185}{365}$ per day. The $\$200$ purchase accrues interest for $9$ days.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 200\left(1 + \dfrac{0.185}{365}\right)^{9} \\ &= 200.91 \end{aligned}$$
Add the $\$149$ purchase.
$$200.91 + 149 = 349.91$$
This balance accrues interest from 13 April to 30 April, $18$ days (both included).
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 349.91\left(1 + \dfrac{0.185}{365}\right)^{18} \\ &= \$353.12 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the balance after the second purchase and applies interest again, or equivalent merit
Finds the first compounded amount, or equivalent merit

Steven has a credit card with an interest rate of 12.80\% per annum compounding daily and an interest free period of 30 days. Any interest is charged for both the date of purchase and the date of payment.

Steven purchases a bicycle on the 15th of October for \$1405.95 and has made no repayments.

What does Steven owe in total on his credit card on November 30th?

solutions.latex:
The bicycle is not paid for within the 30 interest-free days, so interest is charged from the date of purchase. From 15 October to 30 November, counting both dates, is $17 + 30 = 47$ days.
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= 1405.95\left(1 + \dfrac{0.128}{365}\right)^{47} \\ &= \$1429.31 \end{aligned}$$
This matches option C.

parts.latex:
Aisha used her credit card to buy 1500 shares at a price of \$7.50 per share. A brokerage fee of $1.2\%$ was also charged on the purchase.

At the end of her first year owning the shares, she collected an annual dividend at a yield of $5.5\%$. She then used this dividend to pay back part of her credit card debt.

Calculate the amount Aisha still owes on her credit card given that the interest rate on the credit card is $20\%$ per annum, compounded daily.

solutions.latex:
The cost of the shares includes the $1.2\%$ brokerage fee.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Cost of buying shares}&=1500\times 7.50\times 1.012\\&=\$11\,385\end{aligned}$$
The debt grows for one year at $20\%$ per annum, compounded daily.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Amount owing after one year}&=11\,385\left(1+\dfrac{20\%}{365}\right)^{365}\\&=\$13\,904.91\end{aligned}$$
The dividend is $5.5\%$ of the value of the shares.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Dividend}&=5.5\%\times 1500\times 7.50\\&=\$618.75\end{aligned}$$
The dividend is then paid off the debt.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Amount owing after repayment}&=13\,904.91-618.75\\&=\$13\,286.16\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the dividend paid, or equivalent merit
Finds the amount owing after one year before a repayment is made, or equivalent merit
Finds the cost of purchasing the shares, or equivalent merit

On 20th July, Izabella purchased a Harry Styles concert ticket for \$480 on her credit card. No other purchases were made using this card in July. Simple interest was charged at a rate of $19.74\%$ p.a. There was no interest free period. The period for which interest was charged included the date of purchase and the date of payment.

What amount was paid when the account was paid in full on 31st July?

solutions.latex:
Interest is charged from 20th July to 31st July, including both dates.
$$\text{Number of days} = 31 - 20 + 1 = 12$$
Use the simple interest formula $I = Prn$ with $P = 480$, $r = 0.1974$ per year and $n = \dfrac{12}{365}$ years.
$$\begin{aligned} I &= 480 \times 0.1974 \times \dfrac{12}{365} \\ &\approx \$3.12 \end{aligned}$$
The amount paid is the purchase price plus interest.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Amount} &= 480 + 3.12 \\ &= \$483.12 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Izabella paid } \$483.12$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the interest using 12 days, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Allen has a credit card that charges compound interest at a rate of $21\%$ per annum. The credit card does not have an interest-free period, and interest is charged up to and including the date of payment.

During one week, Allen makes the following transactions.

\extable{2828_q3b_t1}

Allen is due to pay his account in full on 9 November.

What will be the total interest payable on Allen's transactions?

solutions.latex:
Interest is charged up to and including the payment date, with daily rate $\dfrac{21\%}{365}$.

For the $13$ Oct transaction, the number of days to $9$ Nov is
$$(31 - 13 + 1) + 9 = 28$$
$$FV = 30\left(1 + \dfrac{21\%}{365}\right)^{28} = \$30.4871$$
For the $18$ Oct transaction, the number of days is
$$(31 - 18 + 1) + 9 = 23$$
$$FV = 89\left(1 + \dfrac{21\%}{365}\right)^{23} = \$90.1852$$
$$\text{Total} = \$120.67$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Interest} &= 120.67 - 119 \\ &= \$1.67 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Correctly calculates any one future value

parts.latex:
On 10 June, Sam used his credit card to purchase a new washing machine for \$453. No other purchases were made using this card in June. Interest was charged at a rate of 19% per annum compounded daily with no interest-free period. The period for which interest was charged included the date of purchase and the date of payment. The account was paid in full on 30 June.

How much interest was Sam charged?

solutions.latex:
From 10 June to 30 June, including both dates, is $21$ days.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Interest} &= 453\left(1+\dfrac{0.19}{365}\right)^{21}-453 \\ &= \$4.98 \end{aligned}$$

Hence the answer is option C.
criteria: Correct answer

parts.latex:
A total of $\$11.60$ was charged for 29 days interest, calculated on a credit card balance.

If the bank has an annual credit card interest rate of $18.25\%$, what was the credit card balance when the charge was calculated?

solutions.latex:
Simple interest: $I = Prn$, with $I = 11.60$, $r = 0.1825$ per year and $n = \dfrac{29}{365}$ years.
$$\begin{aligned} 11.60 &= P\times 0.1825\times\dfrac{29}{365} \\ 11.60 &= 0.0145\,P \\ P &= \dfrac{11.60}{0.0145} \\ &= 800 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the balance was } \$800$$
criteria: Correct answer
Substitutes correctly into $I = Prn$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Calculate the daily interest of Jacinta's credit card as a percentage. Give your answer correct to three decimal places.

Jacinta is due to pay her account in full on 9 February.

What will be the total interest payable on Jacinta's transactions?

solutions.latex:
The simple interest rate is $21\%$ per annum, and a year has 365 days.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Daily rate} &= \dfrac{21\%}{365} \\ &\approx 0.0575\% \\ &\approx 0.058\% \text{ (3 decimal places)} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{daily interest} \approx 0.058\%$$
criteria: Correct answer

solutions.latex:
Interest is charged from the day of each transaction up to and including 9 February, so the number of days is (days remaining in January, including the transaction day) $+\ 9$.

13 January to 9 February:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Days} &= (31-13+1)+9 \\ &= 28 \end{aligned}$$
18 January to 9 February:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Days} &= (31-18+1)+9 \\ &= 23 \end{aligned}$$
Interest is simple interest, $I = Prn$, with daily rate $r = \dfrac{0.21}{365}$.
$$\begin{aligned} I_1 &= 30\times\dfrac{0.21}{365}\times 28 \approx \$0.48 \\ I_2 &= 89\times\dfrac{0.21}{365}\times 23 \approx \$1.18 \end{aligned}$$
Total interest:
$$\begin{aligned} I &\approx 0.4833+1.1777 \\ &\approx \$1.66 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{total interest payable} \approx \$1.66$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the interest on one transaction, or the number of days for both transactions, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Maggie has a credit card which has no interest free period

Interest is charged at the end of each month at 16.25% per annum, compounding daily, from the purchase date (included) to the last day of the month (included).

There is a minimum payment of 2.5% of the closing balance after the interest is added.

Maggie started the month of June with a zero balance and made purchases of \$150.00 on $6^{\text{th}}$ June and \$245.90 on $20^{\text{th}}$ June.

Calculate the minimum payment due at the end of June.

solutions.latex:
Interest compounds daily, so the daily rate is
$$r=\dfrac{0.1625}{365}\approx 0.000445205$$
June has 30 days. Each purchase earns interest from its purchase date to 30 June, both days included.

$\$150.00$ (6 June): $6$ to $30$ June is $25$ days.

$\$245.90$ (20 June): $20$ to $30$ June is $11$ days.

Using $A=P(1+r)^n$ for each purchase:
$$\begin{aligned} A_1 &= 150(1+r)^{25} \approx \$151.68 \\ A_2 &= 245.90(1+r)^{11} \approx \$247.11 \end{aligned}$$
Closing balance after interest:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Balance} &\approx 151.68+247.11 \\ &= \$398.79 \end{aligned}$$
The minimum payment is $2.5\%$ of the closing balance:
$$\begin{aligned} 0.025\times 398.79 &\approx \$9.97 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{minimum payment} \approx \$9.97$$
criteria: Correct answer
Calculates the closing balance including interest, or equivalent merit
Calculates the interest on one purchase using the correct number of days, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Peter has a credit card with the following conditions:

There is no interest free period.

Compound Interest at the rate of $0.06\%$ per day is charged at the end of each month.

Interest is calculated from and including the date of purchase to the last day of the month.

Peter's credit card statement for August is shown, with some figures missing.

\exfigure{498_q9_1}

The minimum payment is calculated as $5\%$ of the closing balance on 31 August.

Calculate the minimum payment.

solutions.latex:
Interest compounds daily at $0.06\%$ for 12 days (as in the source working).
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Closing balance} &= 4800(1+0.0006)^{12} \\ &= \$4834.67 \end{aligned}$$
The minimum payment is $5\%$ of this:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Minimum payment} &= 0.05 \times 4834.67 \\ &= \$241.73 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the closing balance, or equivalent merit
Substitutes into the compound interest formula, or equivalent merit
